subject: Clarify KMS/HSM choices + log retention requirements
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Shah <anika@finovate.ai>
Cc: Karthis Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify KMS/HSM choices + log retention requirements

Hi Anika —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + a few clarifying questions so we can put a recommended configuration together for your security and procurement teams.

Recap (from our notes):
- You plan to send production PII to Redwood-powered generation endpoints (tokenization on the client side not feasible in short term).
- Finovate requires: in-transit TLS, at-rest AES-256, and the option for customer-managed keys (CMK) with HSM-backed key material.
- Audit requirements: detailed per-request logging (request metadata, model id, per-route token counts) retained for a configurable window; default retention in scope is 12 months, but legal is asking for 2 years for specific workflows.

Clarifying questions for procurement/security so we can finalize:
1) For CMK: do you require Redwood to integrate with your cloud KMS (BYOK) or would you prefer Redwood-hosted keys with customer key-wrapping (Redwood-managed but customer-seeded)?
2) HSM: must the key material reside in your HSM (never exportable), or is an HSM-backed KMS (cloud HSM) acceptable?
3) Scope of logs: which fields are considered regulated PII (we'll treat any payload fields you flag as non-persisted unless you opt-in)? Are you able to provide a short list (field names) we should exclude from long-term retention?
4) Retention SLA: you mentioned 24 months for transaction logs for anti-fraud workflows — confirm whether that applies to raw prompts or just derived telemetry.

Next steps I propose:
- We’ll prepare two recommended configurations (BYOK -> cloud KMS integration; and Redwood-managed with HSM-wrapped CMKs) including impact on latency and on audit exportability.
- Attach a quick one-pager on KMS options and a copy of your questionnaire for us to fill.

I’ve attached the KMS options one-pager and a blank copy of the questionnaire — when you have a moment please indicate your preferred CMK model and retention window.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0214

Attachments: Redwood_KMS_options_onepager.pdf (pdf), Finovate_encryption_questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Anika Shah <anika@finovate.ai>

Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@finovate.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@finovate.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify KMS/HSM choices + log retention requirements

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the succinct recap. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) For CMK: do you require Redwood to integrate with your cloud KMS (BYOK) or would you prefer Redwood-hosted keys with customer key-wrapping (Redwood-managed but customer-seeded)?
We strongly prefer direct integration with our cloud KMS (BYOK). We need the ability to rotate keys from our side and have cryptographic control.

> 2) HSM: must the key material reside in your HSM (never exportable), or is an HSM-backed KMS (cloud HSM) acceptable?
Cloud HSM (e.g., Google Cloud HSM or AWS CloudHSM) is acceptable, but the key metadata must show HSM protection and key export must be disallowed.

> 3) Scope of logs: which fields are considered regulated PII...
We will flag the account_number, ssn_hash (we redact today), and any free-text notes that contain customer identifiers. Those three should be excluded from long-term retention unless explicitly required for a compliance process.

> 4) Retention SLA: you mentioned 24 months...
This applies to transaction-level telemetry (request id, model id, timestamps, outcome codes). Raw prompts containing PII should be retained only as needed for investigations and otherwise purged after 90 days unless legal authorizes extension.

We want a short write-up showing the latency and operational trade-offs for BYOK + CloudKMS vs Redwood-managed wrapped keys, and the approach to exporting audit logs to our SIEM for 2-year retention. Procurement will want estimated delta in price for the BYOK integration.

—Anika
Head of Product Security, Finovate AI

On a logistics note: procurement@finovate.ai will expect a formal answers spreadsheet returned; we’ll upload to your Drive link when complete.

From: Karthis Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika Shah <anika@finovate.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:26:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify KMS/HSM choices + log retention requirements

Tessa / Camila — capturing Security's quick take before we draft the two-option proposal for Finovate. Key items: 

- BYOK (cloud KMS integration):
  * Pros: Customer retains cryptographic control, direct rotation, and aligns with Finovate's policy.
  * Cons: Adds integration work to map Finovate KMS accounts to per-tenant key bindings; latency impact minimal (~5-12ms per request for KMS envelope operations if we perform a per-request decrypt — we recommend envelope encryption with RL (runtime local) cache of DEKs to avoid per-request KMS calls).
  * Ops: We will surface key usage metrics and logs; however, we must clearly document what is exported vs what remains in Redwood logs. Export path: periodic streaming of audit events to Finovate SIEM (Kafka/S3 push) is supported.

- Redwood-managed with customer-seeded key-wrapping:
  * Pros: Lower ops burden, faster onboarding, lower per-request latency (we can do all DEK management inside the runtime).
  * Cons: Loss of direct rotation control — we will implement key rotation hooks and allow rollover but Finovate cannot unilaterally revoke prior DEKs without a formal revoke flow. HSM-backed wrapping can be arranged.

- Logs and retention: we can support per-route retention policies. Implementation approach: redact flagged fields at ingestion, store minimal telemetry for 24 months for specified routes, and export a filtered audit stream to the customer's SIEM. For raw prompt access for investigation, we recommend an access-controlled retention vault with 90-day default purge and manual legal hold procedures.

Action items for our reply to Finovate:
1) Draft the BYOK integration_spec and latency/cost estimate (include envelope encryption recommendation).
2) Draft the Redwood-managed key-wrapping option with explicit revocation/rotation flow and SLA notes.
3) Fill the Finovate questionnaire and return to procurement.

I'll take (1); Camila can draft (2) and she can fill the questionnaire. Tessa — will you confirm pricing delta guidance with sales ops for BYOK?

—Karthis
Director, Security Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Clarify KMS/HSM choices + log retention requirements

Anika — thanks for the clarity. Attached is a short two-option summary and the completed questionnaire (see attached). High-level notes:

- BYOK (cloud KMS): estimated one-time integration engineering effort: 3-4 weeks; operational runbook for rotation + emergency revoke; monthly add-on: $2,500 for key management operations and audit export support (ballpark, subject to legal/pricing review). Latency impact when implemented with DEK caching: +5-15ms p99.

- Redwood-managed (customer-seeded wrap): estimated onboarding 1-2 weeks; lower monthly ops fee (included in Dedicated package); we provide a documented revocation procedure and HSM-wrapping option if you require HSM semantics for key sealing.

- Logs: we configured the sample export to include request id, model id, timestamp, and outcome codes by default. Fields flagged by Finovate (account_number, ssn_hash, free_text_customer_notes) will be redacted from long-term export and retained in the isolated investigation vault for up to 90 days. We will provide a signed data handling attestation for the legal team.

Next steps:
- Marco / procurement: confirm which option you prefer so we can finalize pricing and an SOW.
- Karthis/Camila: please attach the two-option technical appendix and the completed questionnaire to this thread.

Thanks —
Tessa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
